newsitem.title: UK: Scapa sees further stg impact, orders up.
newsitem.headline: Scapa sees further stg impact, orders up.

text.p: Britain's Scapa Group Plc, a supplier of fabrics and roll coverings for the pulp and paper industry, said on Thursday that if the current strength of sterling was maintained, it would continue to have an impact on its results in the current financial year.
The company, however, assured that its order books of the units supplying the paper industry were strong and its new products would help it make further progress in this sector during 1997.
Innovative product development pushed up pre-tax profits of Scapa during the year to March 1997 to 66.5 million stg with its earnings per share rising seven percent to 19 pence.

The company faced a tough 1996 due to sluggish growth in the paper industry in Canada and western Europe. However, it was compensated by significant progress in its technical tapes division, the company said.
Scapa's net debt was down to 79.6 million stg from 100.5 million stg with its gearing down to 31.6 percent from 40.3 percent.
